title: AiAgentBuilder
wrapsNative: NavigationStack; a segmented Picker (.pickerStyle(.segmented)) for Configure and Test in a compact width and an HStack of the two panes in a regular width (horizontalSizeClass); a Form of MonarchTextField, TextField(axis: .vertical), a row that opens MonarchAiConnectorPicker in a .sheet, and MonarchAiKnowledgeScope; a test pane of MonarchAiThread with MonarchAiPromptInput in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)
summary: A recipe, not a component: a screen to define an AI agent (persona, instructions, tools and knowledge) and try the unsaved definition in a test chat.
whenToUse: Admin or builder screens where people create or edit an agent and want to test it before saving.
whenNotToUse: Picking an existing agent: use MonarchAiAgentPicker. Only choosing tools or knowledge for a conversation: use MonarchAiConnectorPicker or MonarchAiKnowledgeScope on their own.
api: if horizontalSizeClass == .regular { HStack(spacing: 0) { form; Divider(); test } } else { VStack { Picker("View", selection: $pane) { Text("Configure"); Text("Test") }.pickerStyle(.segmented); if pane == .configure { form } else { test } } }

form: Form { Section("Persona") { MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent, size: .lg, isDecorative: true); MonarchTextField("Name", text:, error:); MonarchTextField("Role", text:, helper:) }; Section { TextField("Instructions", text:, axis: .vertical) } footer: { "n / 8000 characters" }; Section("Tools") { Button → .sheet { MonarchAiConnectorPicker("Tools", connectors: $connectors, isSearchable: false) } }; Section("Knowledge") { MonarchAiKnowledgeScope(sources, selection: $knowledge) }; Section { Button("Save agent") } }

test: VStack { MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent, state: conversation.isBusy ? .working : .idle); Button("Restart test") { conversation.stop(); conversation.reset() }; MonarchAiThread(conversation.messages, showsDaySeparators: false, empty:).safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { MonarchAiPromptInput("Message the agent", text:) { conversation.send($0, body: ["agent": definition]) } } }

options.name: definition
options.type: App state: name, role, instructions, tool permissions ([MonarchAiConnector]), knowledge ids
options.description: Held by the app and saved on Save agent; every edit clears the saved message, as the web's onChange does.

options.name: connectors
options.description: The tools the agent may use, grouped by connector with a permission per tool (allow, ask, never), edited in MonarchAiConnectorPicker in a sheet from the Tools row. Destructive tools cannot be set to allow unless the app passes allowsDestructiveAutoApprove.

options.name: sources
options.description: Knowledge the agent can read, as a MonarchAiKnowledgeScope tree. Leave the section out without sources.

options.name: conversation
options.description: The test chat. Each test message is sent with the current definition in body under "agent", so the transport runs the unsaved agent. Leave the Test pane out without it.

options.name: maxInstructions
options.description: Longest instructions; the field is cut to it and its section footer counts characters.

options.name: save
options.description: Save agent checks the name, then the app saves; the section footer reads Agent saved and VoiceOver announces it.

states.name: iPhone
states.description: Configure and Test are a system segmented control under the navigation bar; the form scrolls in Configure and the test chat fills Test.

states.name: regular width
states.description: On iPad the form and the test chat show side by side with a system divider.

states.name: name missing
states.description: After Save agent with an empty name, the name field shows "Give the agent a name." as its error and nothing is saved.

states.name: saved
states.description: The Save section's footer reads Agent saved until the next edit.

states.name: testing
states.description: The avatar reads working while the reply runs; Restart test stops and clears the test conversation.

states.name: empty test
states.description: The thread shows "Send a message to try the agent."

appearance: Every part is an existing component or system control: a system Form with section headers and footers, MonarchTextField, the system multi-line TextField, MonarchAiConnectorPicker, MonarchAiKnowledgeScope, MonarchAiAgentAvatar, MonarchAiThread, MonarchAiPromptInput, a Monarch ghost button and the system segmented control and divider. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components and the system controls.
platformNotes: The web ships AiAgentBuilder as one component with the form and the test chat side by side, stacked on narrow screens. On iOS it is a recipe drawn as the web draws it on a narrow screen: one column, the form and then the Test panel below it. Android uses Material 3 primary tabs and switches at 840dp. The fields are a system Form, so section headers and footers carry the headings and the character count. The web's tool checkbox list is MonarchAiConnectorPicker, opened in a sheet from a Tools row because it is itself a searchable List in a NavigationStack and cannot be nested in the Form; the definition sends the allowed and asked tool ids. Instructions use the system TextField with axis: .vertical because MonarchTextField is single line. The web's avatar URL field is the app's own picker beside MonarchAiAgentAvatar, since Monarch loads no images. The web's save promise with progress and error is the app's own call; this recipe shows the saved state as a section footer with a VoiceOver announcement and the missing name as the field's error. The web moves focus to the name field when the name is missing; this recipe does not move focus.
accessibility: Persona, Instructions, Tools and Knowledge are Form section headers; Test is a header in the test pane.
The name field shows its error as text and reports it through MonarchTextField.
The character count is the Instructions section footer.
Agent saved is written in the Save section footer and announced without moving focus.
Configure and Test are a system segmented control with the selected state.
The avatars are decorative; the agent's name is in the name field and the navigation title.
edgeCases: Keep the test thread out of the scrolling Form: on iPhone it is its own segment, on iPad its own pane.
A test send while a tool call waits for approval is refused and the text comes back into the prompt input.
Edits after a save clear the saved message, so it never claims an unsaved edit was saved.
Long instructions are cut to the limit, including pasted text.
Switching segments keeps the test conversation and the draft, because both are state above the panes.
